page: Microsoft Azure F48as_v7 is a virtual machine instance from the Fasv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 4.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing connection to external high-performance storage volumes.

Benchmark results place the F48as_v7 in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, as well as PassMark CPU and physics tests. The AMD EPYC processor architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration, resulting in top-tier performance in PassMark extended instructions and bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is also highly competitive, with write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth scoring in the top tier, while large-block read bandwidth remains strong.

This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, database operations, and web serving, as evidenced by top-tier Redis SET operations and PassMark database benchmarks. It also demonstrates strong capabilities for small to medium LLM inference tasks, though performance drops to average levels when processing larger 70B models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means users must rely on external network-attached storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff to consider for I/O-heavy applications.
